summary: The narrator, weakened and disoriented, leaves her room in a dark hallway intending to say a last farewell to Tz'ac Tzotz, one of Sarah's children. She meets Marcelina, who will not reveal where Sarah is, and the narrator then finds the baby's room empty, realizing the children have likely been taken. The main power then fails, plunging the hallway into darkness as heavy boots approach up the stairs.
one_line: A disoriented narrator searches for Tz'ac Tzotz and Sarah in a darkened compound as the children are taken and boots approach.
key_facts: The narrator quietly pulled back the door and peered into a dark hallway that was empty, with no snakes, and only a light breeze flowing through.
The narrator decided that what she really wanted to do first and foremost was see Tz'ac Tzotz one last time.
Marcelina, wearing a white shift, told the narrator that everyone was praying for her and that it was almost time.
Marcelina said Sarah had been looking forward to the ceremony and wanted them to bring her.
When asked where Sarah was, Marcelina did not know or would not say; the narrator was told only that the people there loved Sarah and were taking good care of her.
Marcelina whispered "It's our life" and turned her face away when the narrator asked her to promise to stop all of this.
The narrator took her passport and a charge card from her bag and slipped them into her pants pocket.
The narrator found the room where Tz'ac Tzotz and his mother were empty, with the crib also empty.
The narrator feared Alex Goddard might materialize and pulled away from Marcelina without another word.
The narrator realized she had been a fool not to head straight for the lab.
The main power abruptly died, or was deliberately shut off, plunging the room and hallway into pitch darkness.
Heavy boots were heard pounding up the steps as the scene ends.

entities.name: Sarah
entities.role: woman whose children are Tz'ac Tzotz and another child; her whereabouts are unknown to the narrator
